newsitem.title: FRANCE: Napoleon vaunts Eurostar to get away from Waterloo.
newsitem.headline: Napoleon vaunts Eurostar to get away from Waterloo.

text.p: France's defeated Emperor Napoleon advises travellers between Britain and France to use Eurostar high-speed trains "to leave Waterloo as fast as possible".
An advertisment in French newspapers on Wednesday showed a dejected-looking Napoleon vaunting Eurostar's Channel Tunnel service between London's Waterloo International station and Paris.
The station was named after the 1815 Battle of Waterloo, near Brussels, in which an alliance of British, Prussian and Austrian troops defeated the French emperor's army, forcing him from the throne.
Ironically, it was Napoleon who first proposed digging a tunnel under the Channel -- to invade England.
